With regard to the proposed expansion of terminal areas, these carriers argue that such expansion would make them more competitive with private and contract carriage. The service areas of regular-route carriers will be expanded enabling them to serve more shippers in a larger, but economically related service area, thus improving their operating efficiencies. Local and short-haul carriers with authority described in terms of cities will have larger service areas and will be less dependent upon interline pickup and delivery traffic tendered by long-haul carriers. Some carriers argue that only regulated carriers should be allowed to serve the expanded zones. Other carriers urge that the expanded population-mileage formula be applied only to carriers' terminal areas. The difference between these two concepts is that commercial zones are areas totally exempt from economic regulation under section 203(b)(8) of the Act, whereas the Commission exercises jurisdiction over terminal area operations through regulation of the line-haul movement pursuant to section 202(c) of the Act. Terminal area expansion would not eliminate Commission control over entry, service requirements, or rates. Other carriers argue that expansion of terminal areas without a concomitant expansion of commercial zones would lead to discriminatory business practices, serious financial harm to local cartage firms, and unfair advantage to long-haul carriers.
